findings.description: The 'How adopters can verify' section of v1.0.1.md (line 42) still describes the old conditional-guard behavior that was present at R1 HEAD but was eliminated in fix-round-1: 'If a runner already has pyyaml / jsonschema importable from its preinstalled Python environment, the conditional if ! python3 -c import yaml skip is taken, no install runs, and no hash check happens — same green-path behaviour as v1.0.0.' Fix-round-1 (SAFE-MAJ-002 closure) replaced all conditional install guards with unconditional installs followed by version-pin assertions. The conditional skip path NO LONGER EXISTS in the v1.0.1 code. The release notes are now factually incorrect: they describe a behaviour that was removed in this very slice's fix-round-1. An adopter reading the release notes before pin-bumping to v1.0.1 would incorrectly believe that a runner with preinstalled pyyaml 6.0.1 still skips the hash-verified install, when in fact the unconditional install now runs and the version-pin assertion will fail (pyyaml 6.0.1 != 6.0.2) — causing an explicit error annotation rather than a silent bypass.
findings.recommendation: Replace line 42 of docs/releases/v1.0.1.md with accurate text describing the current unconditional install + version-pin assertion behavior. Suggested replacement: 'The install step is unconditional — the workflow always runs pip install --require-hashes regardless of runner-preinstalled state. Following the install, a version-pin assertion (assert yaml.__version__ == "6.0.2"; assert jsonschema.__version__ == "4.23.0") confirms the pinned versions are active. If a hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner has pyyaml 6.0.1 preinstalled from apt, the unconditional install will upgrade it to 6.0.2 via user-site; if the hash-mismatch assertion fails for any reason, the workflow emits an SCP-E001 annotation and exits non-zero.'
findings.rationale: Release notes are a public surface per VERSIONING.md 'Tag-cut procedure'. Shipping release notes that describe a conditional skip that was removed in the same fix cycle is a documentation-accuracy defect that will confuse adopters who inspect the release notes to understand v1.0.1's security posture. This is materially worse than the original COMP-MIN-002 concern (which was about an undocumented gap) — it is an active misstatement of current behavior. Must be resolved before the v1.0.1 tag is cut.

findings.description: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 'Lockfile regeneration procedure' (lines 1058–1067) describes the pip-compile command and says 'Review the diff (transitive deps may also bump), file the version change as a PATCH or MINOR per VERSIONING.md.' It does NOT mention the obligation to update the version-pin assertions in the workflow files (yaml.__version__ == '6.0.2' and jsonschema.__version__ == '4.23.0') when bumping the top-level pins in requirements/policy-check.in. As of fix-round-1, these assertions are hardcoded in .github/workflows/policy-check.yml (at lines 648, 742, 1099) and in release-gate.yml. A maintainer following the documented regeneration procedure — editing policy-check.in, regenerating policy-check.txt, reviewing the diff, filing the version bump — would correctly update the lockfile but leave the version-pin assertions pointing to the old version numbers, causing every CI run to fail with 'pinned-version assertion failed: yaml=6.0.3 expected 4.23.0' (or similar) until someone discovers the undocumented second step. This is a maintenance-path completeness gap introduced by fix-round-1's addition of the version-pin assertion pattern. Package review item 6 identifies this exact concern.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to the regeneration procedure in ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 after the pip-compile code block: 'After regenerating, also update the version-pin assertions in .github/workflows/policy-check.yml (assert yaml.__version__ == "X.Y.Z"; assert jsonschema.__version__ == "A.B.C" — currently three assertion sites at lines ~648, ~742, ~1099) and .github/workflows/release-gate.yml (~line 119) to match the new top-level pins from requirements/policy-check.in. The version-pin assertions and the lockfile pins must be kept in lockstep.' Alternatively, extract the version constants to a dedicated variable or env block to eliminate the multi-site update obligation — but that is a more invasive refactor appropriate for v1.1.
findings.rationale: The version-pin assertion pattern (added in fix-round-1 to close SAFE-MAJ-002) creates an undocumented post-regeneration step: updating the hardcoded version strings in 4 workflow locations. Failure to document this creates a trap for any maintainer following the documented regeneration procedure, and it creates a supply-chain governance risk: a PIN bump that correctly updates the lockfile but leaves stale assertions in the workflow files will cause CI breakage discovered only at runtime. Per the review package examination item 6, this MIN must be filed.

findings.description: D-038 rationale (filed at original R1 HEAD ee32abc) describes the install mechanism as '--require-hashes via lockfile' but does not mention the unconditional install pattern or the version-pin assertion, which were introduced in fix-round-1. The D-038 rationale says 'All three layers — Python deps, OPA-family binaries, GitHub Actions SHA pins — are now hash-anchored at SCP source' — this characterisation is accurate but the D-038 text does not disclose that the install is now unconditional (not conditional on import presence) or that a version-pin assertion is enforced post-install. Per package review item 7, a D-038 amendment is likely not required because fix-round-1 refines the implementation without changing the decision's shape (hash-pinned install via lockfile remains the core resolution), but the absence of the unconditional-install rationale from D-038 means the decision row and the ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 description are the canonical source of truth for the implementation detail.
findings.recommendation: No mandatory amendment to D-038. If the operator wishes, a single appended sentence to the D-038 rationale field would close the gap: 'Fix-round-1 (post-R1 review) strengthened the install from conditional (import-presence guard) to unconditional with version-pin assertion — see SAFE-MAJ-002 closure in FIX-ROUND-1.md.' This is cosmetic; D-038 remains ACCEPTED and accurate at the decision level. File as NIT only.
findings.rationale: The decision row records the decision to adopt hash-pinned installs; the implementation refinement (unconditional + version-pin assertion) is an execution detail documented in FIX-ROUND-1.md and ADOPT-001 §12.7.13. Per governance norms, implementation refinements within a single fix round of the same slice do not require a new decision row or D-038 amendment unless the threat model changes. No new threat surface was introduced; SAFE-MAJ-002 corrected the mechanism to be more effective at the same decision. Cosmetic NIT only.
